                "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...\n\nPeace River At Arcadia at SR 70 affecting DeSoto County.\n\n* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHERE...Peace River at Arcadia at SR 70.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 16.0 feet, Up to 60 homes at River Acres are flooded.\nThe Woman's Club and American Legion are impacted.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 8:30 AM EST Saturday the stage was 16.0 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending\nat 8:30 AM EST Saturday was 16.4 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall to 12.4 feet Thursday\nmorning.\n- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.\n- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 16.0\nfeet on 09/12/1988.\n- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
                "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nMotorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars\nthrough flooded areas.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\nThe next statement will be issued this evening at 915 PM EST.",

                "instruction": "There is a high risk of rip currents.\n\nRip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away\nfrom shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the\nsandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties\nand piers.                 "description": "* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, High astronomical tides\nwill cause minor flooding in low lying areas around Humboldt\nBay.                 "headline": "Flood Watch issued November 6 at 8:17PM CST until November 9 at 12:00PM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX",
                "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.\n\n* WHERE...A portion of south Texas, including the following areas,\nAransas Islands, Bee, Coastal Aransas, Coastal Kleberg, Coastal\nNueces, Coastal Refugio, Coastal San Patricio, Duval, Goliad,\nInland Kleberg, Inland Nueces, Inland Refugio, Inland San Patricio,\nJim Wells, Kleberg Islands, La Salle, Live Oak, McMullen, Nueces\nIslands and Webb.\n\n* WHEN...From Saturday afternoon through Monday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Widespread forecast rainfall amounts of 2-4 inches will be common\nacross South Texas with high end amounts approaching 5 inches.\nIsolated amounts exceeding 5 inches remains a possibility,\nespecially in the vicinity of training and slow moving storms.\nWhile soils will be able to absorb most of this moisture, the\nhigher rainfall rates can quickly lead to localized, urban\nflooding and in locations with poor drainage.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",

                "headline": "Flood Warning issued November 6 at 8:21PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL",
                "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...\n\nSt Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.\n\n.Exceptional rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River has\ncaused Moderate flooding at the gauge west of Cocoa.
